children: President Donald Trump dismissed mounting warnings about artificial intelligence, arguing that slowing development could jeopardize the United States’ lead over China, Bloomberg News reported.

“We’re leading China in AI. We’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins,” Trump told reporters Sunday at the Irish Open. “And we can put guardrails. We can do this and that. But I think you have a lot of negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn’t be bringing it up.”
His comments followed a call from Anthropic
CEO Dario Amodei to give safety measures more time to catch up with increasingly capable AI models. OpenAI
chief Elon Musk backed the proposal, which includes allowing independent experts greater access to evaluate frontier systems.
National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett

AI safety as a manageable problem and said voluntary industry safeguards could provide a workable model. Other administration allies have argued that product-liability laws and market pressure already give companies incentives to prevent harmful or unpredictable behavior.

Lawmakers from both parties are discussing guardrails, although they remain divided over whether government regulation or industry cooperation should take the lead. Democrats are pushing for stronger oversight while Republican leaders have emphasized protecting innovation and maintaining the country’s technological advantage.

The disagreement raises policy uncertainty for richly valued AI stocks and the companies supplying chips, data centers and electricity to the sector. A voluntary approach would likely preserve rapid capital spending and model development. Binding testing rules, independent audits or restrictions on advanced models could raise compliance costs and delay product launches. Investors also face the larger question of whether enormous AI infrastructure budgets will generate returns quickly enough to justify current valuations.
Trump, however, showed little interest in allowing the warnings to derail development.
“They’re bringing up things that won’t happen, but whoever wins, with AI, wins,” Trump said..

title: Trump rejects calls for AI slowdown, citing race with China
